per_claim.claim_text: Across this literature, precipitation effects are estimated at aggregate spatial scales (network-wide, city-level, or at most corridor-level) .
per_claim.source_quote: Research surveying the impacts of climate change on the transport sectors has been conducted at a national and multi-regional scale in several developed countries.
per_claim.reasoning: Wang 2020 discusses spatial scale in terms of general research coverage — studies conducted at 'national and multi-regional scale' — and separately lists precipitation as a climate parameter causing flooding, delays, and road closures (Table 3). The paper never states that precipitation effects are estimated specifically at 'aggregate spatial scales (network-wide, city-level, or at most corridor-level).' Those three scale labels do not appear together or in that framing anywhere in the paper. The citing paper has attributed a characterisation of precipitation-effect estimation granularity that Wang 2020 does not make.
